svg.title: Envelope detection two ways: rectify and low-pass, or the Hilbert transform
svg.desc: Top row: a raw waveform of three fading bursts is rectified (every negative half-cycle flipped positive), then low-pass filtered. The result is the envelope, a little late and with some ripple left from the carrier. Bottom row: the same waveform goes through a Hilbert transform; the magnitude of the analytic signal, the square root of x squared plus H{x} squared, is the envelope directly, with no carrier ripple and no delay, drawn above and below the waveform. Any filter after it can be much gentler. Adapted from Burnett-Thompson (2007).
svg.text: 1. Rectify, then low-pass filter (the classic diode detector)
2. Hilbert transform, then magnitude (no carrier ripple, no delay)
